channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Refrigeration hack hit about 700 French supermarkets; Forescout now counts nearly 13,000 exposed refrigeration control services worldwide
item.description: On 22 October Forescout reported 12,976 internet-exposed refrigeration management services in 99 countries — the class of web-managed controller attackers forced into continuous defrost at French supermarkets on the nights of 11–13 October. France’s finance minister put the toll at about 700 stores, including Carrefour, E.Leclerc, Intermarché and Monoprix; the Paris prosecutor says fires also resulted and is investigating with ANSSI. CERT-FR names Danfoss AK-SC and AK-SM controllers plus Copeland and Dixell XWEB, and its 16 October revision says the campaigns are probably still under way. Most affected units are end-of-life, and the EU Cyber Resilience Act will not compel fixes for them. No actor, CVE or entry route has been named, and no new attack nights have been reported since 13 October. - Forescout Vedere Labs (22 Oct 2026); CERT-FR alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 (v1 12 Oct, v2 13 Oct adding Copeland and Dixell XWEB, v3 16 Oct); The Record (20 Oct 2026); SecurityWeek (15 Oct 2026); AP via News4JAX (13 Oct 2026); Danfoss statement (12 Oct 2026) - Attacks on the nights of 11–13 Oct 2026, none reported since; latest CERT-FR revision 16 Oct 2026 (campaigns probably still ongoing); updated 22 Oct 2026 with Forescout exposure data — investigation ongoing

item.title: [High] The FortiOS flaw behind Unit 42’s Peerstitch case enters CISA KEV, after a FortiManager compromise exposed more than 500 managed firewalls
item.category: Incident report — Unit 42 analysis of a telecom managed-service-provider intrusion via FortiManager (CVE-2024-47575) and FortiOS (CVE-2025-61624, in CISA KEV since 16 Oct); cluster CL-STA-0954, no state named
item.description: CISA added CVE-2025-61624, a FortiOS command-line path-traversal flaw, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 16 October, two days after Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 described its use. In that case attackers exploited FortiManager (CVE-2024-47575) at a telecommunications managed service provider and took configuration and credential material for more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls; Unit 42 calls this exposure, not confirmed intrusion into those customers’ networks. They then used CVE-2025-61624 to get root on managed FortiGates and drop the Peerstitch loader, and wiped logs and rogue accounts. Unit 42 tracks the cluster as CL-STA-0954 (also UNC5820); it overlaps with suspected nation-state intrusions, but no state is named. Fortinet fixed the flaw in April and rates it Medium because it needs privileged access. The CVE record also lists Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808, which runs FortiOS, as affected. - Unit 42 (Palo Alto Networks) report (14 Oct 2026); Fortinet advisory FG-IR-26-122; CISA KEV catalog; The Hacker News (16 Oct 2026); Industrial Cyber - Unit 42 report 14 Oct 2026; added to CISA KEV 16 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Ransomware crews are now using the PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication bypass to get past MFA and into networks, including utilities, energy and manufacturers
item.category: Incident report — Unit 42 update: ransomware crews (Qilin, Inc and Settra) exploiting the PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication bypass CVE-2026-0257, in CISA KEV since 13 May 2026
item.description: Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 updated its brief on 19–20 October to report that ransomware operators are exploiting CVE-2026-0257, an authentication bypass in the PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal and gateway, to start VPN sessions without valid credentials and bypass MFA. Unit 42 ties the activity to Spikey Scorpius (Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius (Inc), and public reporting also names Settra. Exploitation was first seen in June, after a proof of concept appeared on 29 May; the flaw was fixed in May and added to CISA’s KEV catalog on 13 May. Targeted sectors include utilities and energy, manufacturing, and transportation and logistics. After entry the crews use remote-management tools, move over RDP and SMB, and in one case pivoted to vCenter, disabled security controls on ESXi hosts and dumped credentials from a domain controller’s virtual disk. No OT impact is reported. - Unit 42 (Palo Alto Networks) brief, updated 19–20 Oct 2026; Help Net Security; CISA KEV catalog - Ransomware use reported 19–20 Oct 2026; in KEV since 13 May 2026 — re-warned on new ransomware activity

item.title: [High] CISA, the FBI and partners warn that SafePay ransomware has hit at least 600 organizations since August 2024
item.category: Advisory — joint advisory AA26-293A from CISA, the FBI, the US Secret Service and German and UK partners on SafePay ransomware, which the agencies say has hit at least 600 organizations across multiple critical-infrastructure sectors
item.description: Advisory AA26-293A, issued on 20 October by CISA, the FBI and the US Secret Service with Germany’s LKA Rheinland-Pfalz, the UK National Crime Agency and the North West Regional Organised Crime Unit, says SafePay has hit at least 600 organizations from multiple critical-infrastructure sectors in North America, South America, Europe and Australia. Entry is usually through exposed or brute-forced credentials, phished accounts, VPN logins from Mullvad addresses and automated exploitation of edge-device flaws; the group then steals data, deletes shadow copies, resets network-attached storage that holds backups and moves with tools such as WinRM, PsExec and RDP. The advisory carries indicators and ATT&CK mappings for activity from November 2024 to August 2026. It names no victims, and reporting on it describes no OT, energy or water impact, so the OT risk here is the usual one: a ransomware crew reaching the IT network that plant systems depend on. - CISA advisory AA26-293A (20 Oct 2026), as reported by BleepingComputer and Cybersecurity Dive - Published 20 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] Albert Heijn restarts home deliveries after the Ahold Delhaize cyberattack; the group confirms malicious activity, and stores stayed open
item.category: Incident — cyberattack on a major grocery group’s IT and online services that disrupted logistics; not a confirmed OT compromise (Food & Ag-adjacent)
item.description: Albert Heijn restarted grocery home deliveries on 23 October, nearly two weeks after Ahold Delhaize took systems offline on 12 October across most of its brands in Europe and the US (NL Times). In its latest statement, on 19 October, the group said outside experts had confirmed “malicious actions of others”, that it had notified the Dutch NCSC and filed a police report, and that it had no evidence so far that sensitive data was taken; stores stayed open throughout. Stop & Shop and Hannaford sites were back on 20 October, according to the company as quoted by the Boston Globe; no restoration status has been confirmed for Food Lion or Giant. Albert Heijn said its distribution centres had to be restarted on 13–14 October (as reported by NL Times). No attacker or ransomware claim is known. This was an IT-side attack that disrupted logistics, not a confirmed OT compromise, and the Dutch NCSC saw no link to the French refrigeration attack. - Ahold Delhaize statements (12, 13–14 and 19 Oct 2026); NL Times (15 and 23 Oct 2026); Boston Globe (20 Oct 2026); SecurityWeek (20 Oct 2026) - Systems offline 12 Oct 2026; malicious activity confirmed 19 Oct 2026; Albert Heijn deliveries restarted 23 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] A third Citrix NetScaler zero-day is exploited, and a fourth critical flaw was patched on 9 October
item.category: Incident — three NetScaler zero-days confirmed exploited, state-sponsored actors suspected by Mandiant (not attributed); a fourth critical flaw patched 9 Oct, no exploitation reported
item.description: Citrix has confirmed a third NetScaler zero-day under attack, days after patching two others that were exploited for weeks before disclosure, and on 9 October it shipped a fourth fix. The exploited trio is CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772 and CVE-2026-88779; the federal KEV deadline for the newest passed on 7 October. The earlier pair brought web shells, rogue admin accounts and stolen configurations, and patching does not evict an intruder. The new CVE-2026-107406 (CVSS v4.0 9.5) is a SAML memory overflow that could allow code execution; no exploitation is reported, but appliances patched last week need another upgrade. Shadowserver counts more than 20,000 internet-exposed NetScaler fingerprints. Because NetScaler often fronts remote access into plant networks, an unhunted appliance is a possible foothold toward OT. - Citrix security bulletins CTX697096 and CTX697174 (and the 9 Oct bulletin for CVE-2026-107406); CISA KEV catalog; Dutch NCSC; Tenable, watchTowr, LevelBlue, Arctic Wolf and Mandiant/GTIG research; reported by SecurityWeek, BleepingComputer, The Hacker News, Cybersecurity Dive and Help Net Security - Fourth flaw CVE-2026-107406 patched 9 Oct 2026, no exploitation reported (The Hacker News, 9 Oct); CVE-2026-88779 fixed 3–4 Oct and added to KEV 4 Oct 2026 (deadline 7 Oct, now passed); watchTowr denial-of-service finding and CISA/Australian warnings 5 Oct 2026 (SecurityWeek and The Record, 5 Oct); first two flaws confirmed and patched 27 Sep 2026, mass exploitation after a 28 Sep proof-of-concept write-up; post-exploitation analysis 1 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Ivanti warns attackers chained three zero-day flaws, one still unpatched, to take root on fully patched Connect Secure VPNs
item.category: Incident — Ivanti Connect Secure VPN zero-day chain exploited on fully patched appliances since early Oct; new actor UTA0576 tracked by Volexity; one flaw still unpatched; no OT victim named
item.description: Ivanti disclosed on 13 October that a small number of customers were hit through a chain of three zero-day flaws that gave unauthenticated, root-level code execution on fully patched Connect Secure appliances. Volexity, which found it while investigating a customer incident, dates its case to 3 October (other researchers saw activity from 1 October) and tracks a previously undocumented actor, UTA0576. The intruders stole domain credentials stored on the appliance, searched Active Directory for LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys, sprayed passwords and scanned internal networks, but left no web shell or backdoor. Volexity judges, with low confidence, that the group is financially motivated, and, with medium confidence, that it uses AI models for exploit development. Fixes cover two of the flaws (CVE-2026-104935); the third, a privilege-escalation bug, is still unpatched. VPN gateways like this commonly sit at the IT/OT boundary. - Ivanti advisory and Volexity research, as reported by SecurityWeek (13 Oct 2026) - Disclosed 13 Oct 2026; added to CISA KEV 13 Oct 2026; exploitation observed from 3 Oct 2026 — third flaw still unpatched (no public fix or CVE found as of this edition)

item.title: [Info] Booz Allen: frontier AI models went from a perimeter breach to a control-zone action in just over 16 minutes in a lab test
item.category: Research — Booz Allen Hamilton lab test of frontier AI models moving from an IT foothold into an industrial control environment
item.description: Booz Allen’s 8 October report, From Digital to Physical: The AI Threat Is Here, describes tests in its isolated OT lab in Chantilly, Virginia, modelled on a manufacturing facility. Frontier models from several unnamed vendors met all eight test objectives, going from a perimeter compromise to energising an output on a controller in just over 16 minutes, with a human required to approve every exploit and physical action. One agent found a robotic arm’s API, gained admin access and moved the arm, and a SCADA gateway holding live authenticated sessions to 14 devices gave the models a ready path. Some controls held: one controller rejected a stop command, and local-control mode blocked a remote motor start. Booz Allen calls the results preliminary; some known flaws were left unpatched on purpose and no zero-days were developed. Its Kyle Miller told Dark Reading that removing the approval step would likely have roughly halved the time. - Booz Allen Hamilton report (8 Oct 2026); Dark Reading (16 Oct 2026); Industrial Cyber - Report published 8 Oct 2026; Dark Reading coverage 16 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] AI-agent ransomware toolkit “Phantom” used edge and remote-access flaws against industrial, manufacturing and energy targets
item.category: Threat Intel — SOCRadar analysis of AI-assisted ransomware intrusions aimed mainly at industrial, manufacturing and energy organisations
item.description: SOCRadar researchers, reported by The Hacker News on 23 October, found an exposed directory showing affiliates of the INC and The Gentlemen ransomware groups running intrusions through an AI-agent framework called Phantom, with a human operator writing prompts and reviewing each step. Entry came through internet-facing systems such as FortiClient EMS, SimpleHelp, cPanel and VPN gateways, and one reused password opened VPN, backup, remote-management and security platforms. SOCRadar estimates about 62 organisations were targeted, most of them in the US, and four appeared on leak sites. The activity is IT-side data theft and extortion; the report describes no access to controllers or SCADA, but the same edge entry points and reused credentials are what an attacker needs to reach OT-adjacent networks. - The Hacker News, citing SOCRadar (23 Oct 2026) - Published 23 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] Accenture, Dragos and SANS launch a $10 million programme to put OT monitoring in up to 500 small utilities
item.category: Programme — Accenture, Dragos and SANS launch the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation for small utilities
item.description: The Community Cyber Resilience Foundation, announced on 20 October by Accenture, Dragos and the SANS Institute with Elastic providing technology support, offers free OT security help to small water, wastewater, electric and natural gas utilities with under $100 million in annual revenue. Dragos describes it as a US programme; the foundation’s own site also mentions Canada. Participants get the Dragos Platform, Neighborhood Keeper and OT-CERT; Accenture assessment, deployment and ongoing support; SANS training with GIAC certification; and hardware funding where needed. About $10 million in funding and services covers a first phase of up to 500 utilities, on top of the 100-plus already in Dragos’s Community Defense Program, and enrollment “opens soon”. It is a resource announcement, not a threat report, but it reaches the small operators that have struggled to fund OT monitoring (editorial assessment). - Dragos announcement (20 Oct 2026); Community Cyber Resilience Foundation site; The Record and Industrial Cyber - Announced 20 Oct 2026; enrollment opens soon

item.title: [High] Siemens confirms a Software Center flaw is being exploited to deliver malware, and CISA adds it to the KEV catalog
item.category: Advisory — Siemens Software Center uncontrolled search-path (DLL side-loading) flaw CVE-2026-110936 (CVSS v3.1 6.7 / v4.0 8.4) exploited in the “Romulus” ClickFix campaign; in CISA KEV since 20 Oct 2026
item.description: Siemens first published CVE-2026-110936 on 15 October and on 19 October confirmed it is being exploited. Software Center, the tool engineers use to install and update Siemens software, did not restrict where it searches for helper DLLs, so attackers paired a genuine, validly signed copy with their own malicious libraries in an installer package. Siemens ties the activity to the “Romulus” multi-platform ClickFix campaign, which tricks users into running pasted commands, and names no final malware family. It says no Siemens system, product or update channel was breached, to its knowledge. Version 4.0.9.8 fixes the flaw, and installed copies update on next start. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 20 October with a 3 November deadline and has republished Siemens’ advisory as ICSA-26-295-03. Exploitation needs local access and a user who runs the lure, so engineering workstations running Siemens tooling are the exposure. - Siemens ProductCERT advisory SSA-580366 and blog (19 Oct 2026); CISA KEV catalog and advisory ICSA-26-295-03; SecurityWeek (19 Oct 2026) - Disclosed 15 Oct 2026; exploitation confirmed 19 Oct 2026; added to KEV 20 Oct 2026 (federal deadline 3 Nov 2026)

item.title: [High] PHP2Shell is now confirmed in OT products: Siemens, Schneider, ABB, HMS, Belden and Johnson Controls list affected gear, some with no fix yet
item.category: Advisory — PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, CVSS v4.0 9.2): Siemens, Schneider, ABB, HMS, Belden and Johnson Controls list affected products; working shells seen on honeypots, no confirmed OT compromise
item.description: PHP2Shell is a pair of unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in PHP (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, CVSS v4.0 9.2) fixed on 21 October in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Exploitation attempts began 17 October and now run into the millions; on 24 October honeypots recorded 35 working shells, but CISA reports no confirmed successful exploitation and no second-stage payload or victim has been reported. On 26 October SecurityWeek tallied the industrial vendor responses. Siemens lists RUGGEDCOM APE1808 units running PAN-OS (SSA-566512) with no patch, only Palo Alto workarounds. Schneider has fixed Security Expert (1.48.4.0) but offers only mitigations for EcoStruxure Control Engineering. ABB lists MES installations with DokuWiki and the APROL process control system (patches expected 26 and 29 October). HMS Netbiter and Talk2M, Belden NetModule NRSW (no patch; disable the web interface) and Johnson Controls Illustra cameras are also affected. Rockwell and Hitachi Energy were still assessing, and Moxa reports no impact. Software that bundles PHP is easy to miss in IT patch sweeps (editorial assessment), so ask OT vendors directly. - SecurityWeek (26 Oct 2026) summarizing Schneider SESB-2026-295-01, Siemens SSA-566512, ABB SA26P015, HMS, Belden and Johnson Controls advisories; Industrial Cyber (26 Oct 2026); The Hacker News (25 Oct 2026) - Exploitation attempts since 17 Oct 2026; PHP fixes 21 Oct 2026; Schneider bulletin 22 Oct 2026; honeypot-confirmed shells 24 Oct 2026; vendor roundup 26 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] October ICS fixes: critical ICONICS GENESIS64 flaws and a WAGO controller bug join Siemens, Rockwell and ABB, and some Siemens flaws still have no fix
item.category: Advisory — October ICS advisories: CISA’s 22 Oct republication of Siemens’ 13 Oct advisories, its 20 Oct batch (WAGO, Moxa), Mitsubishi Electric ICONICS GENESIS64 (15 Oct), Rockwell 1732E ArmorBlock and ABB dynovaPRO; no exploitation reported
item.description: On 22 October CISA republished Siemens’ 13 October advisories (ICSA-26-295-02 to -18): fixes are still pending for the S7 PLC web server, the S7-1500 MFP Linux subsystems and WinCC V7.5, and none is planned for APOGEE MBC/MEC. CISA’s 20 October batch covered WAGO controller firmware (CVE-2026-80466, CVSS v3.1 8.8: a low-privileged user can inject commands that run as root; fixed in 4.10.0/FW32) and Moxa’s AIG-302 edge gateway (hard-coded key CVE-2026-109813, v3.1 8.1 / v4.0 8.6; fixed in 1.4.1). Mitsubishi Electric’s 15 October advisory fixes an authentication bypass (CVE-2026-16436, v4.0 9.2) and over-permissive DCOM defaults (CVE-2026-16438, v4.0 9.4) across ICONICS GENESIS64, GENESIS, Hyper Historian and related products; MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz get no fix. Earlier in the month Rockwell fixed a critical 1732E ArmorBlock admin-takeover flaw and ABB a dynovaPRO password-reset flaw. None is reported exploited. - CISA ICS advisories ICSA-26-293-02 and -03 (20 Oct 2026) and ICSA-26-295-02 to -18 (22 Oct 2026); Mitsubishi Electric advisory 2026-006 (15 Oct 2026); SecurityWeek ICS Patch Tuesday (14 Oct 2026), summarizing Siemens ProductCERT, Rockwell, Schneider Electric and ABB releases - Siemens, Rockwell and ABB releases 13–14 Oct 2026; Mitsubishi Electric 15 Oct 2026; CISA batches 20 and 22 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] BeyondTrust patches a Remote Support zero-day exploited since late August by a suspected China-nexus espionage actor
item.category: Advisory — BeyondTrust Remote Support authentication-bypass zero-day (BT26-05), exploited since late August by a suspected China-nexus actor; vendor remote-access tooling often used to reach plant systems; no OT victims named
item.description: BeyondTrust has fixed CVE-2026-102764, an authentication bypass in self-hosted Remote Support appliances (version 26.2.3 and earlier) that lets an unprivileged remote attacker perform file operations. Mandiant and Google’s threat-intelligence group link the exploitation to a suspected state-sponsored espionage actor they track as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221); CrowdStrike calls it Warp Panda. After getting in, the intruders used web shells, escalated to root, wiped logs and harvested stored credentials for lateral movement. SaaS customers were patched on 8 October; self-hosted customers must patch themselves. Shadowserver counts more than 1,400 exposed instances, and Google expects opportunistic exploitation to follow. No victims are named, and none is reported in critical infrastructure. Integrators and OEMs often use this class of tool for vendor access to plants, so its owners should check it. CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog on 16 October with a three-day deadline. We did not find a CVSS score, so none is given. - BleepingComputer (16 Oct 2026); The Record; BeyondTrust advisory BT26-05; Mandiant/GTIG and CrowdStrike research as relayed by these outlets - Reported 16 Oct 2026; exploitation since late Aug 2026; SaaS patched 8 Oct 2026; added to CISA KEV 16 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] Coast Guard issues NVIC 02-26 on maritime cybersecurity plans and IT/OT risk assessments, with a 16 July 2027 deadline
item.category: Regulation — US Coast Guard Navigation and Vessel Inspection Circular (NVIC) 02-26 guides maritime operators on cybersecurity officers, assessments and plans under 33 CFR Part 101 Subpart F; no CVE
item.description: The US Coast Guard released NVIC 02-26, a companion to its maritime cybersecurity rule, for operators of US-flagged vessels, port facilities and Outer Continental Shelf facilities regulated under the Maritime Transportation Security Act. It explains how to name a cybersecurity officer, complete a cyber risk assessment and write a Cybersecurity Plan for Coast Guard approval; all three are due by 16 July 2027. The approach is performance-based: operators choose how to meet each requirement, but must back claims with documentation and observable evidence, and a plan that only restates the regulation must also explain how it is met. Penetration testing is not needed for the first submission but is expected periodically over five-year renewal cycles, with attention to OT safety. Enclosures cover plan development, a sample officer letter, penetration-testing guidance and an optional NIST CSF method for scoping IT and OT systems. - US Coast Guard NVIC 02-26 (dated 19 Oct 2026), as reported by Industrial Cyber - Reported 23 Oct 2026; assessments, officer designations and plans due 16 Jul 2027

item.title: [Info] FERC staff publish CIP audit lessons: unregistered new generation, stacked low-impact systems and AI tools in CIP networks
item.category: Regulation — FERC staff report on CIP audit lessons learned flags late registration of new generation, aggregated low-impact systems and AI tools inside CIP networks; no CVE
item.description: On 13 October FERC released a staff report drawing on its fiscal-2026 audits of NERC-registered entities. Most cybersecurity processes reviewed met the mandatory CIP standards, but auditors found three recurring problems. Some generator owners registered new resources late or never identified their BES Cyber Systems, and several inverter-based resources were running commercially without the required cyber evaluation, one more than a year past the threshold. Two entities treated systems as low impact that together met the medium-impact criteria once affiliate and contractor control was counted. Auditors also saw what the report calls “super intelligence” (SI) tools — chatbots, assistants and automated analytics — appearing inside CIP-networked environments, where they can mimic user behavior and open unauthorized access or lateral-movement paths faster than compliance programs adapt. The report is staff guidance, not a new requirement, and it suggests NERC may consider further guidance or standards changes. - FERC staff report Lessons Learned from Commission-Led CIP Reliability Audits, as reported by Industrial Cyber - Published 13 Oct 2026; Industrial Cyber coverage 15 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] Centrii warns low-impact grid sites to prove NERC CIP-003-9 vendor remote access controls before auditors ask
item.category: Regulation — NERC CIP-003-9 vendor remote access controls for low-impact BES systems (in effect since 1 April 2026); audit-readiness warning; no CVE
item.description: In a 26 October analysis, compliance firm Centrii says CIP-003-9, in effect since 1 April 2026, now requires owners of low-impact bulk electric system assets that allow vendor remote access to have three processes: identify vendor remote access, disable it, and detect known or suspected malicious communications tied to it. The standard does not define “vendor”, and ReliabilityFirst expects auditors to read it broadly, including staff augmentation. Centrii flags records as the weak spot: evidence must be kept for three calendar years, audits of low-impact requirements can reach back six, and the proof is often scattered across email, equipment-maker support portals and contractor systems. The owner stays accountable even when operations are outsourced. Centrii recommends one named person to approve each vendor access path, one to disable it and one place for records. This is a vendor’s compliance commentary, not a regulator statement. - Centrii analysis, as reported by Industrial Cyber - Published 26 Oct 2026; CIP-003-9 in effect since 1 Apr 2026
